purpose: Picture-led owner-feedback teaching guide for Opus and other agents. No model fine-tuning and no new level edits.
source_policy: Original images are unchanged. SVG viewports crop only for presentation; numbered boxes are explanatory overlays. No AI-generated replacement screenshot is used.

boards.title: Finished pieces can still make a bad scene.
boards.subtitle: Cube clutter: the problem is the relationship between the parts, not a lack of small details.
boards.takeaway: REMOVE THE UNRELATED PROP; do not strip all detail from the platform.
boards.evidence: Owner rejected cube/UFO clutter. Boxes identify my interpretation of that complaint; source is an editor capture.
boards.owner_feedback_paraphrase: Objects in cube/UFO make no sense; there are too many things for no reason.
boards.assistant_interpretation: The rod bundle and adjacent cabinet crowd an already established scene. Retain the coherent platform and improve its surfaces.

panels.label: OWNER SCREENSHOT · cropped to remove the editor buttons

notes.title: Extra rod bundle
notes.body: It occupies the space beside the orb. Its role is unclear next to the existing fan and press.

notes.title: One more cabinet
notes.body: Another narrow box competes with the same focal area. Detail alone does not justify it.

notes.title: Keep a clear unit
notes.body: The suspended platform already has a casing and support. Detail that assembly on purpose.

boards.title: Decoration stopped before the level did.
boards.subtitle: The white/default area is a coverage defect. These views have different cameras; compare coverage only.
boards.takeaway: CHECK THE LAST HAZARDS and the fade timing, not just the middle of the section.
boards.evidence: Left: owner editor capture. Right: Refined diagnostic response; no claim of a matched native before/after.
boards.owner_feedback_paraphrase: There is a white part that was not decorated.
boards.assistant_interpretation: Cover the final hazards and delay the factory fade. A nice central frame cannot prove that the complete section is finished.

panels.label: BAD · default area and bare hazards

notes.title: Abrupt boundary
notes.body: The factory background ends while the route continues.

notes.title: Unfinished hazards
notes.body: The end pieces lose the established material treatment.

notes.title: Continue the room
notes.body: Keep the same depth behind the tail of the section.

notes.title: Finish every casing
notes.body: Inspect the final hazard skins and the master fade.

boards.title: The ship feels like one built environment.
boards.subtitle: Preserve the old ship treatment the owner asked to restore; judge its structure, not renderer artifacts.
boards.takeaway: THE SILHOUETTE LEADS; surface detail and heat support it.
boards.evidence: Owner asked to restore the old ship. Refined atlas diagnostic of the retained treatment; not native-play proof.
boards.owner_feedback_paraphrase: I liked the ship, so change that back to the old one.
boards.assistant_interpretation: Continuous fitted edges, panel detail inside the walls and recognizable furnace openings give the route a coherent setting.

notes.title: Continuous edge
notes.body: The metal rim follows the change in slope. The route has a deliberate silhouette.

notes.title: Detail on surfaces
notes.body: Plate seams and vents sit within the wall mass. They are not loose objects in the route.

notes.title: Readable furnace
notes.body: Bars, housing and heat form one machine. Light has a visible source.

boards.title: Keep the parts with a recognizable identity.
boards.subtitle: Wave and early robot were specifically liked. That does not approve every old spike or orb in these images.
boards.takeaway: PRESERVE THE COMPOSITION; repair the weak component locally.
boards.evidence: Owner liked wave and robot. Refined wave / Afterburn robot diagnostics; historical components are labeled.
boards.owner_feedback_paraphrase: I really like the wave and the robot part, but the rest is still pretty bad.
boards.assistant_interpretation: Retain their structural idea, dark depth and localized heat. Later custom spike/orb work can improve components without replacing the scene.

panels.label: WAVE · fitted rails and a recessed fan

notes.title: Route has a strong shape
notes.body: Continuous rails follow the angular corridor.

notes.title: A distinct room landmark
notes.body: The fan adds factory scale behind the play space.

notes.title: Objects belong together
notes.body: Chain, platform and furnace read as one setup.

notes.title: Heat stays localized
notes.body: Dark masonry makes the warm source feel brighter.

boards.title: Do not answer “too basic” by filling the air.
boards.subtitle: UFO: extra infrastructure competes with a route that already contains many hazards.
boards.takeaway: ADD DETAIL TO EXISTING BODIES before adding another background machine.
boards.evidence: Owner rejected UFO clutter. Cyan lines and selection colors are editor UI, not decoration to reproduce.
boards.owner_feedback_paraphrase: The cube/UFO are too crowded and many objects appear to have no reason.
boards.assistant_interpretation: Classify gameplay hazards, their skins and background machinery separately. Remove redundant decoration, not source gameplay.

panels.label: OWNER SCREENSHOT · UI excluded where possible

notes.title: Too many focal edges
notes.body: The huge fan and the foreground hazards compete. More detail is not always more depth.

notes.title: Another vertical bundle
notes.body: Extra rods and cabinets make the room busier without making its function clearer.

notes.title: Do not delete the route
notes.body: Separate source hazards from added skins and props before removing anything.

boards.title: More screen coverage did not make better fire.
boards.subtitle: Two rejected experiments: a decorative frame, then large repeated flame shapes. Neither is the baseline.
boards.takeaway: MATCH THE MATERIAL AND MOTION, not only the percentage of the screen covered.
boards.evidence: Historical CLOSING-FIRE / ENGULFED diagnostics. Static atlas views cannot establish native animation quality.
boards.owner_feedback_paraphrase: The fire should close in and eventually engulf the player, but these results looked poor; the first was preferred over the later version.
boards.assistant_interpretation: A mechanical coverage target missed scale, repetition, color and integration. Repeated oversized flames look pasted on the scene.

notes.title: The rectangle dominates
notes.body: The regular straight border reads as framing.

notes.title: Repetition becomes texture
notes.body: Uniform tiny flames do not imply a spreading fire.

notes.title: Scale overwhelms the scene
notes.body: Large rounded motifs flatten the factory depth.

notes.title: Coverage is only one check
notes.body: Closing the gap is not proof of convincing fire.

boards.title: Turn an outline into a fitted material.
boards.subtitle: Compare the spike treatment. These are historical diagnostics at different scales, not a pixel-diff test.
boards.takeaway: KEEP THE ORIGINAL HAZARD; fit a non-colliding skin to its silhouette.
boards.evidence: Outline spikes were criticized. Steel skins are retained in CUSTOM-ORBS; native collision still needs native testing.
boards.owner_feedback_paraphrase: The spikes are not decorated; the spike and block designs are too basic.
boards.assistant_interpretation: Use a dark steel face, inset edge, restrained bevel and mounting seam. Do not enlarge the invisible hazard to match new art.

notes.title: The face stays visually empty
notes.body: Bright triangle edges do not describe a material.

notes.title: Glow carries the whole design
notes.body: Increasing brightness would keep the same weakness.

notes.title: Give the blade a face
notes.body: Steel planes and an inset edge create a solid object.

notes.title: Fit the platform edge
notes.body: Keep teeth aligned with the casing and original bounds.

boards.title: Custom art should preserve the interaction.
boards.subtitle: Pressure switches belong to the factory, while the original orb logic remains underneath.
boards.takeaway: HIDE ONLY THE NATIVE VISUAL CORE; keep its gameplay and shared motion.
boards.evidence: Owner explicitly kept custom orbs. Custom diagnostic; data invariants are verified by the baseline validator.
boards.owner_feedback_paraphrase: Keep custom orbs but undo the custom portals.
boards.assistant_interpretation: Keep the pressure-switch casing attached to its parent. Separate visual alpha from toggling gameplay; retain native portal appearance.

notes.title: A mounted switch
notes.body: A complete casing, inset face and warm signal read as part of the machine.

notes.title: Keep native behavior
notes.body: Group 1157 hides only eight native orb cores using Alpha. Do not Toggle them off.

notes.title: Carry the attachments
notes.body: The press and its fitted art move together. A skin must not remain behind.

boards.title: A rollback can apply to just one component.
boards.subtitle: The latest feedback kept custom orbs and reverted custom portals. Treat those as separate decisions.
boards.takeaway: KEEP CUSTOM ORBS + NATIVE PORTALS. Do not treat either image as blanket approval.
boards.evidence: Explicit owner rollback. Left: reverted Custom portal. Right: older Refined native appearance restored in baseline.
boards.owner_feedback_paraphrase: Okay, keep custom orbs but undo the custom portals.
boards.assistant_interpretation: Track the latest decision for each component. The owner originally requested custom portals, then reverted them while keeping custom orbs; do not label an entire revision approved or rejected.

notes.title: The portal was reverted
notes.body: The later feedback changed the portal decision only.

notes.title: Do not reuse it by accident
notes.body: Old Custom-era previews contain reverted portals.

notes.title: Native appearance remains
notes.body: Keep its original visual language and restrained trim.

notes.title: The orb decision is separate
notes.body: Keep the pressure switches shown in picture 08.

boards.title: Good-looking art can still break the level.
boards.subtitle: The following blue orb shared a group with later objects. Separate behavior before adding more attached art.
boards.takeaway: AUDIT MEMBERS AND TRIGGER TARGETS. A free-looking number is not proof of a free group.
boards.evidence: Data diagram from examples/blue-orb-group-fix.json and project-state.json; not a gameplay screenshot.
boards.owner_feedback_paraphrase: Later objects seemed to disappear; the blue following orb was moving objects with the same group ID. Organize the build into editor layers.
boards.assistant_interpretation: The fix must isolate the moving assembly, preserve the later pulse, and distinguish editor organization from render depth.

boards.title: Prototype one purposeful assembly first.
boards.subtitle: SCHEMATIC DESIGN STUDY · not new game art, not an applied level change, not owner-approved.
boards.takeaway: WHAT I SHOULD HAVE DONE: review one supported machine before repeating it across a section.
boards.evidence: Assistant retrospective proposal. Diagram illustrates mounting and detail placement, not a finished GD asset.
boards.assistant_interpretation: Instead of responding with a large prop pass, first test one coherent casing with support, bounded detail and preserved negative space.
boards.success_check: At gameplay scale, identify the machine function and supports without explaining every prop. Preserve original collision and empty route.

boards.title: Test atmosphere as a sequence, not a still.
boards.subtitle: SCHEMATIC MOTION STUDY · proposed checks for ash, machinery and readability; no native animation is claimed.
boards.takeaway: WHAT I SHOULD HAVE DONE: check movement extremes, native camera and cost before calling it finished.
boards.evidence: Assistant retrospective proposal. Dots/arrows/frames are teaching diagrams; no new effect is added to the baseline.
boards.owner_feedback_paraphrase: The atmosphere should be darker with more realistic burning ashes; decoration should include moving elements.
boards.assistant_interpretation: Start with small dim irregular flakes and motion attached to believable machinery. Test several moments and measure performance before scaling up.
boards.proposal_status: unbuilt; does not restart discarded fire experiments
boards.success_check: Capture actual game states with camera/time/aspect recorded; inspect interactions, moving attachments, exit coverage and performance.
